StringLength

Returns a string length.

Syntax:

StringLength(<String>)

Parameter:

  • String. Type: String. The source string.

Example:

String(Contractors.Address)

Substring

Extracts a substring from a string.

Syntax:

Substring(<String>, <Position>, <Length>)

Parameters:

  • String. Type: String. The source string. If the first parameter is a string, the result is a string (it can have zero length). If the first parameter is NULL, the function result is also NULL. If the first parameter is a value of any other type, the function returns an error.
  • Position. Type: Number. The character position where the substring begins.
  • Length. Type: Number. The substring length.

Example:

SUBSTRING(Counterparties.Address, 1, 4)

TrimL

Trims insignificant characters to the left of the first significant character in a string.

Syntax:

TrimL(<String>)

Parameters:

  • String. Type: String. The source string.

Return value:

  • Type: String. The string resulting from trimming spaces.

TrimR

Trims insignificant characters to the right of the last significant character in a string.

Syntax:

TrimR(<String>)

Parameters:

  • String. Type: String. The source string.

Return value:

  • Type: String. The string resulting from trimming spaces.

TrimAll

Trims insignificant characters to the left of the first significant character in a string, and spaces to the right of the last significant character in a string.

Syntax:

TrimAll(<String>)

Parameters:

  • String. Type: String. The source string.

Return value:

  • Type: String. The string resulting from trimming spaces.

Left

Selects the first characters from the left of a string.

Syntax:

Left(<String>, <CountOfCharacters>)

Parameters:

  • String. Type: String. The source string.
  • CountOfCharacters. The Number type. The number of characters to select. Negative values are considered to be zero. If there are fewer characters in the source string than in the parameter, the source string is returned.

Return value:

  • Type: String. The string of selected characters.

Right

Selects the first characters from the right of a string.

Syntax:

Right(<String>, <CountOfCharacters>)

Parameters:

  • String. Type: String. The source string.
  • CountOfCharacters. The Number type. The number of characters to select. Negative values are considered to be zero. If there are fewer characters in the source string than in the parameter, the source string is returned.

Return value:

  • Type: String. The string of selected characters.

StrFind

Finds the first occurrence of the search string as a substring in the source string. The search is not case-sensitive.

Syntax:

StrFind(<String>, <SearchSubstring>)

Parameters:

  • String. Type: String. The source string.
  • SearchSubstring. The String type. The search substring.

Return value:

  • Type: Number (the length is 12). The position found, starting from 1. If it returns 0, the string is not found.

Upper

Converts all characters in a string to uppercase.

Syntax:

Upper(<String>)

Parameters:

  • String. Type: String. The source string.

Return value:

  • Type: String. The string resulting from the conversion.

Lower

Converts all characters in a string to lowercase.

Syntax:

Lower(<String>)

Parameters:

  • String. Type: String. The source string.

Return value:

  • Type: String. The string resulting from the conversion.

StrReplace

Finds all occurrences of the search substring in the source string and replaces it with the replacement substring.

Syntax:

StrReplace(<String>,<SearchSubstring>,<ReplaceSubstring>)

Parameters:

  • String. Type: String. The source string.
  • SearchSubstring. Type: String. The search substring.
  • ReplaceSubstring. Type: String. The substring to replace the search substring with.

Return value:

  • Type: String. The string resulting from the replacement.

    If the second parameter is a constant, the string length is:

    <String> + (<String> / <SearchSubstring> rounded up) * (<ReplaceSubstring> - <SearchSubstring>), but not less than the length of <String>.

    If the second parameter is not a constant, the string length is equal to the length of <String> * <ReplaceSubstring>.

    If the resulting length is greater than 1024, then this is a string of unlimited length.

NStr

Gets a string in the current user language or in the specified language from a set of strings in different languages available in the configuration.

Syntax:

NStr(<String>, <LanguageCode>)

Parameters:

  • String. Type: String. Strings in different languages separated by ";" (semicolon). The string in one language consists of the language code specified in the metadata, the symbol "=" (equal to), and the text string in this language in single quotes, double quotes, or without quotes (when only one language is specified).
  • LanguageCode. Type: String. The code of the language in which you need to get the string. If the value is not specified, the string will be in the language defined for the current user.

Return value:

  • Type: String. The string corresponding to the specified language or the language of the current user.
